title: Rates, confidence and AD

predict.q: The central bank cuts the interest rate from 5% to 3%. Nothing else changes. What happens on the AD/AS diagram?

options.s: AD shifts right, as investment rises at every price level.
options.fb: Cheaper borrowing makes more projects worth doing, so I rises at every price level: AD1 → AD2.

options.s: A movement down along AD, because borrowing is cheaper.
options.fb: Movements along AD come only from changes in the price level; a change in I shifts AD.

options.s: Only AS shifts right, because firms' costs fall.
options.fb: The main effect is on spending; AS is not the curve that moves here.

options.s: Nothing, because most firms use their own savings.
options.fb: Retained profits have an opportunity cost: the interest they could earn.

task: Move the interest rate slider from 5% to 3%, then the business confidence slider, and watch AD.

target.do: Cut the interest rate to 3%, then press Check.

takeaway: A change in I, for any reason, shifts AD.
explore: Lower confidence shifts AD left; a rate cut with confidence at −2 gives a smaller net shift.
